elements.evidence: "IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license"

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf

elements.evidence: No perpetuity language; licence endures only until "expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3"
"Such license is irrevocable except upon expiration or termination of this Agreement" — irrevocability is qualified, not absolute for paid-up licences

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: Termination hook is any "expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3", not limited to uncured material breach
No assignment/succession language anywhere in the rendered clause
"IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates ... a nonexclusive license" (covered outright, exceeding the notice condition)

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: Rendered clause contains no transfer or successor provision

offending_extra_words: Such license is irrevocable except upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3.
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but three preferred elements fail: no perpetuity/unqualified irrevocability for paid-up licences, no limitation of termination to uncured material breach, and no transferability to successors.
Fallback is also incomplete: affiliate coverage is present (indeed broader than notice-conditioned), but the M&A successor transfer right is absent, so neither bargain is complete.

Minimality fails: deleting "revocable" alone achieves the no-at-will-revocation outcome; the added sentence "Such license is irrevocable except upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 3." is duplicative surplus (official gate: 23 words to 47, ratio 2.04).

Intent risk: capitalised "Affiliates" is not shown as a defined term in the resolved definitions, and the new cross-reference to "Section 3" is unverified, introducing a potentially dangling term/mechanic.

Actionable fix: keep the single operator edit (strike "revocable", insert ", its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf"), define or lower-case "affiliates", and add a short successor-transfer phrase rather than a new irrevocability sentence.
